flagged.evidence: The title says “Fixed-bin calibration estimates underestimate,” but the Statement only proves the underestimation inequality when d is additionally jointly convex. For K=2, let d(p,q)=(p₁−q₁)²(1−(p₁−q₁)²), use the single bin Δ₂, and put equal mass on (G,r(G))=((0,1),(1,0)) and ((1/2,1/2),(1/2,1/2)), with Y conditionally distributed as r(G). This is a valid calibration function; d is continuous, nonnegative, and zero on the diagonal. The expected calibration error is 0, while the bin value is d((3/4,1/4),(1/4,3/4))=3/16. Thus the fixed-bin limit can overestimate calibration error, contrary to the unqualified title.
